notes.meaning: A person who keeps refusing correction becomes stubborn like an ox that resists the plow. In the end, such a person will be broken suddenly, like clay pottery smashed beyond repair. God warns people patiently through many voices, but those who stubbornly ignore Him will eventually face ruin without any cure.

When good and godly leaders are in charge, the whole community is happy and thrives. But when wicked people take power, citizens groan under unfair burdens and fear what will happen next. Good leadership brings peace and justice that everyone can see and celebrate.

A young person who pursues godly wisdom brings great joy to his parents. In contrast, someone who wastes time and money on immoral living will quickly lose everything he owns. Choosing God's wisdom is the best safeguard against habits that destroy our lives and resources.

A king makes his nation strong and secure when he rules with fair laws and honest courts. But a ruler who demands bribes or heaps unfair taxes on the people tears the country down. A stable society depends on leaders who love justice rather than dishonest gain.

When someone uses fake praise or smooth talk, he is setting a trap for his neighbor. Flattery is often meant to trick people or puff up their pride so they let down their guard and fall. It is wise to be careful around praise that seems designed to take advantage of us.

Wicked people get caught in the traps made by their own sins and end up miserable. But those who live uprightly walk in freedom and safety, having a clear conscience before God. Because God watches over them, they can sing with real joy and peace.

Righteous people take the time to understand the legal rights and needs of the poor, making sure they get fair treatment. Evil people, however, do not care about the struggles of the needy because they see no personal profit in helping them. True goodness always shows thoughtful concern for those who cannot defend themselves.

People who mock what is holy and stir up trouble can set an entire town on fire with anger and division. On the other hand, wise and calm leaders step in to cool tempers and prevent violence. Making peace protects the whole community from disaster.

When a wise person takes a foolish person to court or tries to reason with him, the argument never ends well. The fool either throws a temper tantrum or laughs scornfully, refusing to listen to reason. It is often useless to debate someone who has no desire to find the truth.

Violent and bloodthirsty people hate anyone who lives an honest and blameless life, because goodness exposes their wickedness. In contrast, upright people step forward to protect and care for the lives of those being attacked. Good people seek to defend the innocent rather than harm them.

A fool lets all his temper spill out immediately, saying whatever angry thoughts cross his mind. A wise person shows self-control by holding his anger back and keeping calm inside. Learning to master our temper saves us from saying things we will regret.

When a government leader is willing to believe lies and flattery, all his helpers quickly become corrupt too. The people serving him learn that dishonesty is rewarded, so they tell him only what he wants to hear. Leaders must love the truth if they want an honest administration.

The poor person and the greedy oppressor seem to have nothing in common, yet both receive the gift of life and sight from the Lord. God causes His sun to shine on both, and each one must answer to Him as their Maker. Knowing God sees all people reminds us that He is the ultimate Judge over how we treat others.

When a ruler faithfully defends the rights of the poor and ensures they receive fair trials, his government will stand secure. Rich people can usually hire help, but the poor need an honest ruler to protect them from being cheated. God honors and establishes leaders who care for the helpless.

Careful correction and loving words of instruction help a child learn wisdom. But a child who is left alone to do whatever he pleases will end up bringing shame and heartbreak to his family, especially his mother. Guiding children early keeps them from growing up wild and undisciplined.

When wicked people increase in number and influence, wrongdoing spreads like a disease through the land. Even so, God's people do not need to despair, because they will live to see the sudden ruin of evil. God's justice will always have the final word in human history.

Parents who patiently discipline and guide their children will later enjoy deep rest and quiet minds. A child taught to follow what is right brings great joy and satisfaction to his father and mother. Faithful training early in life pays off with peace in the home later on.

Here vision means God's revealed message through His prophets and teachers. Where people do not hear or heed the word of God, they lose all moral restraint and run wild. Those who listen to God's teaching and obey it find true safety and lasting happiness.

other.label: Popular modern teaching
other.view: Many modern church leaders apply this verse to organizational leadership, teaching that churches and ministries must create clear vision statements and strategic plans to survive.

notes.meaning: A stubborn and rebellious worker cannot be corrected by mere talk. Even if he understands exactly what he is told to do, he refuses to listen or obey unless he faces real consequences. Words alone will not change someone whose heart is set on defying authority.

A person who blurts out words without thinking shows foolish self-confidence. There is actually more hope for an ordinary, dull fool to learn wisdom than for a hasty, know-it-all speaker. Taking time to think before we speak protects us from utter foolishness.

When a master spoils and pampers a servant from childhood, that servant will eventually become insolent and act like the heir of the house. Overindulging someone who needs clear guidance makes him forget his place and refuse to show respect. True kindness requires fair boundaries rather than careless pampering.

A person with a short temper is constantly stirring up arguments and fighting with others. Uncontrolled rage drives people to extremes and leads them into many other sins, like cursing and cruelty. Keeping calm prevents a spark of anger from turning into a blaze of trouble.

A person full of pride will eventually be brought low and humbled, because boasting repels people and offends God. But someone with a humble and lowly spirit will receive lasting honor and respect. Lowering ourselves in humility is the true road to lasting honor.

Anyone who partners with a thief acts as his own worst enemy and damages his own soul. When placed under oath in court, he stays silent instead of telling the truth, bringing guilt and punishment upon his own head. Hiding crime out of loyalty to criminals only drags a person down with them.

Being afraid of what people think or can do traps a person into compromise and sin. But anyone who places his trust in the Lord is lifted high above danger into a place of complete safety. Trusting God frees our hearts from the pressure to please or fear other people.

Many people try hard to win the favor of powerful rulers to get what they want in life. Yet true justice and a person's final outcome come from the Lord alone, not from human courts or politicians. We should look to God as our ultimate judge and provider rather than depending on human power.

Good people who love God find dishonest and wicked ways deeply offensive. At the same time, wicked people despise anyone who lives an honest and godly life because it exposes their own wrongdoing. There is an inescapable divide between following God and chasing after evil.
